issues.description: Inconsistent getter naming for StockIngredient across artifacts: the template repository defines/getters named getIngredientName() and Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getIngredientName(), while the solution repository uses getName() in StockIngredient and Stock.findStockIngredient() calls getName(). The problem statement asks students to "add getters for all the private fields" but does not specify the exact method name, leaving ambiguity. This mismatch can confuse students about which getter name to implement and may lead to failing references in code or tests if the expected method name differs.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the getter name for the StockIngredient.name field consistent across all artifacts. Preferably update the template to use public String getName() (and have Stock.findStockIngredient call getName()), or explicitly state in the problem text which getter name students should implement (getName() or getIngredientName()) and make the template and solution match that choice.

issues.description: The getter for the StockIngredient name is inconsistently named across artifacts: the template repository defines getIngredientName(), while the solution repository uses getName(). The problem statement asks to "add getters for all the private fields" without specifying a name, which leads to an ambiguous expectation. This discrepancy means students reading the template will see getIngredientName() but the intended/reference solution and many idiomatic examples use getName(), creating avoidable mapping confusion when locating and using the name getter (e.g., in Stock.findStockIngredient and other lookups).
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent getter name for the StockIngredient name across all artifacts. Prefer the conventional getName() (rename getIngredientName() to getName() in the template and update all call sites such as Stock.findStockIngredient to use getName()). Also clarify in the problem statement that standard getter names (e.g., getName, getPrice, getQuantity) are expected.
